legend: Jack the jolly jester lives on an undirected tree with n%%ZSMJ0%% vertices, conveniently numbered 1%%ZSMJ1%% through n%%ZSMJ2%%. At the i%%ZSMJ3%%-th (1≤i≤n%%ZSMJ4%%) vertex, there is a jazz jellyfish with a jubilance value of ai%%ZSMJ5%%.

Jack plans to take a jovial jaunt throughout the joyful junctions. He will choose a starting vertex s%%ZSMJ6%% and an ending vertex e%%ZSMJ7%%, then walk along the unique path from s%%ZSMJ8%% to e%%ZSMJ9%%. It is allowed for s=e%%ZSMJ10%%.

Let the vertices he visits be v1,v2,…,vℓ%%ZSMJ11%% in order (so v1=s%%ZSMJ12%% and vℓ=e%%ZSMJ13%%). Because Jack is a perfectly normal human, the total jubilance he gets from walking through this path is defined in the most natural possible way. It will be f(av1,av2,…,avℓ)%%ZSMJ14%%, where f%%ZSMJ15%% is defined as follows:
Note that the path from s%%ZSMJ20%% to e%%ZSMJ21%% may have a different weight from the path from e%%ZSMJ22%% to s%%ZSMJ23%% — we consider these paths to be distinct.
Find the maximum possible jubilance over all paths in the tree.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ24%%, the number of vertices in the tree (2≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ25%%).
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ26%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ27%%, the labels of the vertices (1≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ28%%).
The next n−1%%ZSMJ29%% lines contain two integers ui%%ZSMJ30%% and vi%%ZSMJ31%%, the edges of the graph (1≤ui,vi≤n%%ZSMJ32%%).
output: Print a single integer — the maximum jubilance of a path in the tree.
